curriculum_stages.name: Beginner - Hit or Stand
curriculum_stages.description: Learn the fundamental actions of Hit and Stand. Agent should learn basic hand values and when to take a risk vs. play it safe. No dealer upcard awareness required yet; focus on player's hand.

curriculum_stages.name: Intermediate - Dealer Awareness
curriculum_stages.description: Introduce dealer's upcard consideration. The agent must now learn basic strategy by relating its own hand to the dealer's visible card and deciding whether to Hit or Stand to improve chances of winning. This also reinforce when to hit soft hands and when to stand with hard hands.

curriculum_stages.name: Advanced - Double Down
curriculum_stages.description: Introduce the Double Down action. The agent should learn the optimal conditions to double down based on its hand and the dealer's upcard, capitalizing on favorable situations for higher returns. Understanding when to double down is critical to increasing profitability.

curriculum_stages.name: Expert - Split Hands
curriculum_stages.description: Introduce the Split action. The agent should learn when splitting pairs can significantly improve its odds, based on the specific pair and the dealer's upcard. This requires advanced pattern recognition of situations such as splitting aces and eights versus low-value dealer upcards.

curriculum_stages.name: Early Surrender Strategy
curriculum_stages.description: Early surrender is introduced. Agent should learn that early surrender can cut loses on hands that are statistically unlikely to win. Agent should understand the odds of different dealer upcards and when early surrender makes the most sense.

curriculum_stages.name: Insurance Play
curriculum_stages.description: Introduce the insurance action. Although often a bad bet in the long run, the agent should evaluate when insurance might be advantageous based on card counting or specific game rule variations. Emphasize understanding the probabilities of the dealer having blackjack.

curriculum_stages.name: Master - Full Strategy
curriculum_stages.description: Integrate all actions. The agent must now combine all learned strategies to play optimally across all scenarios. This stage requires fine-tuning decision-making by considering complex interactions between player's hand, dealer's upcard, doubling, splitting, surrender, and insurance under various rules.
